# Watchlight — Developer Edition

> Govern an AI agent in-process, with zero infrastructure. `pip install watchlight` puts a real, fail-closed authorization decision in front of every tool call, sub-agent spawn, and MCP request — the same authorization engine that runs in the Watchlight control plane, embedded as a compiled wheel with an in-memory policy store. No database, no network, no services. When it says `Deny`, it denies for the same reasons production does.

Watchlight Developer Edition (DE) is the open front door to an **Agent Runtime Governance** platform. You decorate a tool with an *intent*, load a [Cedar](https://www.cedarpolicy.com/) policy, and the engine **allows what a policy permits and refuses everything else — before the tool body runs**. It also confines sub-agents to a strict subset of their parent's authority (scope attenuation), and can sit as a policy enforcement point in front of any MCP server. This file orients coding agents to the real, verified API so generated code is correct on the first try.

- **License:** Apache-2.0 (the `watchlight` package). The compiled engine (`watchlight-engine`) and MCP runtime (`watchlight-mcp`) are **free to use, including in production and commercially, for up to 25 governed agents per organization** (a commercial license is required above that, or to re-offer the engine itself as a hosted service).
- **Docs:** https://docs.watchlight.ai/de
- **Repo:** https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de
- **Python:** 3.9+ · prebuilt wheels for Linux, macOS, Windows.

## Install and import (read this before writing imports)

- `pip install watchlight` → import `watchlight` — the `govern` decorator, `govern.scope(...)` attenuation, and the `watchlight dev` dashboard. Pulls in `watchlight-engine` automatically.
- `pip install "watchlight[langgraph]"` / `[pydantic-ai]` / `[claude-agent]` / `[deepagents]` → govern an existing framework agent. In DE these import as submodules: `from watchlight.langgraph import governed_plugin` (also `watchlight.pydantic_ai`, `watchlight.claude_agent`).
- `pip install watchlight-mcp` → import `watchlight_mcp` — the MCP Runtime PEP (`serve`/`serve_background` for HTTP with optional native TLS, `serve_stdio` for stdio-launched servers).
- `pip install watchlight-agent-sdk` → **imports as `watchlight_core`** (the lower-level lifecycle SDK: `InProcessClient`, sessions, preflight, local lineage). There is **no** `watchlight-core` package on PyPI — that module ships *inside* `watchlight-agent-sdk`.
- `pip install "watchlight[all]"` → one install for the whole DE: the SDK (`watchlight_core`) + every framework plugin + the MCP PEP (`watchlight_mcp`). Use this to run any example in the docs without resolving individual packages. (Requires `watchlight >= 0.3.0`.)
- `npm install @watchlight/sdk` → the **TypeScript / Node** lane. `import { govern } from "@watchlight/sdk"` — the same in-process engine (`@watchlight/engine`, compiled to WebAssembly), same API and value-free audit as the Python `watchlight` package, no Python sidecar. See the TypeScript section below.

## Core API — the `watchlight` package (verified, 0.5.0)

- `from watchlight import govern, Denied` — `govern` is a ready-to-use default governor (starts with **no** policies → fail-closed until you load some).
- `govern.load("policies.json")` — load a JSON file: a list of `{"name", "code"}` objects, or `{"policies": [...]}`. A missing file loads nothing (still fail-closed).
- `govern.allow('permit(principal, action == Action::"read", resource);', name="reader")` — add one Cedar policy inline. Chainable.
- `@govern.tool(intent="research")` — decorate a function. On each call the engine authorizes `(agent, intent, "tool/<function_name>")`; on `Allow` the body runs, otherwise it raises `Denied(tool, intent, reason)` **before the body executes**. The resource is always `tool/<function_name>`.
- `Watchlight(agent="my-agent", audit_dir=".watchlight", audit_sink=None)` — construct your own governor instead of the default. `agent` defaults to `$WATCHLIGHT_AGENT` or `"my-agent"`.
- Every decision is appended, **value-free** (no argument values, ever), to `.watchlight/audit.jsonl`.
- `audit_sink=callable` (Python) / `auditSink: (record) => …` (TS `WatchlightOptions`) — an ADDITIVE destination for every audit record (decisions, `sanitization`, `attenuation` — including scopes derived via `govern.scope()`). The sink gets its own copy with EXACTLY the fields the file line carries (frozen in TS); the file stays on and is written first. Fire-and-forget: a returned promise/awaitable is never awaited (Python schedules it on the running event loop; with no loop it is dropped with one warning), and a throw/rejection is reported once (error type only) and never blocks or changes a decision. Reference sinks (Postgres row, OTLP log record, webhook): `examples/patterns/audit-sink.md`.
- `govern.counters(principal, intent=None, resource=None, window="1h", *, outcome="allowed", now=None, max_bytes=64 MiB)` (Python) / `govern.counters({ principal, intent?, resource?, window?, outcome?, now?, maxBytes? })` (TS, synchronous) → `{count, principal, intent, resource, outcome, window: {seconds, start, end}, records, skipped, truncated}`. Folds the LOCAL `audit.jsonl` into a number for a quota policy (`permit(...) when { context.reads_this_hour < 100 }`). Counts only DECISION records (a `decision` and no `event`) matching `principal` (required, exact string, e.g. `User::"u1"`) and, when given, `intent`/`resource` (exact), whose `ts` is in `(now - window, now]` by the record timestamp, not file order. `outcome`: `allowed` = `Allow` (incl. approved); `denied` = `Deny` + `NeedsApproval` holds; `all`. `window`: `"15m"`/`"1h"`/`"24h"`/`"7d"`, bare seconds string, or int seconds; non-positive/malformed raises (`ValueError`/`RangeError`). Streams the file; scans at most `max_bytes` from the END — `truncated: true` = lower bound (omit the counter from `context` so the policy denies, audited — don't throw in the `context` binding, that runs before `authorize` and leaves no record). Lines over 1 MiB or nested >32 deep → `skipped`. Malformed lines → `skipped` (never echoed). Each call RESCANS up to the bound (no cache): rotate the audit file or lower `max_bytes` on long-lived agents; whoever can write the file can reset their quota; concurrent writers → approximate. Missing file → zeros; unreadable → `AuditTrailUnreadable`. The audit sink is never read back. Pure form: `count_audit_records(path, ...)` / `countAuditRecords(path, {...})`. Pattern: `examples/patterns/quotas.md`.

**Minimal complete program (this is the whole pattern — load a policy, decorate, then CALL the tool):**
```python
from watchlight import govern, Denied

govern.allow('permit(principal, action == Action::"research", resource);')  # without this, EVERYTHING denies

@govern.tool(intent="research")
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    return f"results for: {query}"

@govern.tool(intent="transfer")            # governed, but no policy permits it
def transfer_funds(to: str, amount: int) -> str:
    return f"sent ${amount} to {to}"       # never runs — denied first

print(web_search("watchlight docs"))       # ALLOW → the body runs
try:
    transfer_funds("mallory", 1000)        # DENY → raises Denied BEFORE the body runs
except Denied as e:
    print(e)                               # watchlight denied intent 'transfer' on tool/transfer_funds: ...
```
Two mistakes to avoid: (1) decorating a tool WITHOUT loading a policy first — then every call denies (fail-closed by design). (2) defining governed tools but never CALLING them — nothing is authorized and nothing prints. The caller-facing deny `reason` is deliberately uniform and non-revealing — every denial reports `"not authorized"`, never *why* (no matching policy vs forbidden vs a failed condition), so a caller probing the boundary learns nothing to tune against it. The `Denied` message still names the intent + tool (the caller's own request, not a leak); operators reconstruct the true cause from the audit trail / decisionId, never from this string.

## Scope attenuation — confine sub-agents (verified, 0.5.0)

- `scope = govern.scope(tools=[...], resources=[...], intents=[...], max_depth=5, time_budget_seconds=3600)` — the root capability scope.
- `child = scope.attenuate(tools=[...], intents=[...], resources=[...], time_budget_seconds=...)` — derive a **strict-subset** child. Omitting a dimension inherits the parent's. Every `attenuate` runs the real engine strict-subset validation and is audited (streams into `watchlight dev`).
- Raises `AttenuationDenied(violations, reason)` if the child requests authority the parent lacks — `violations` names the overreaching dimension(s) (`AllowedTools`, `AllowedIntents`, `MaxDepth`, `TimeBudget`).
- Raises `DevEditionCeiling(depth)` when a chain would exceed `DE_MAX_DEPTH` (5). This is a product boundary, **not** a policy denial — every level up to it was a real engine-validated subset.
- Import surface: `from watchlight import Scope, AttenuationDenied, DevEditionCeiling, ScopeTokenError, DE_MAX_DEPTH`.
- Cross-process: `token = scope.to_token(ttl_seconds=None)` → `"wls1.<base64url canonical claims>.<base64url HMAC-SHA256>"`; `scope = govern.scope_from_token(token)` in the worker. Requires `Watchlight(token_secret=...)` (≥ 16 bytes) or `WATCHLIGHT_TOKEN_SECRET` — no default; without it both calls raise `ScopeTokenError("no_secret")`. Verification checks the HMAC (constant-time), agent binding, `iat`/`exp` and a lifetime ≤ the scope's time budget, then **replays the whole chain through the engine's strict-subset validator** — a widened chain raises `AttenuationDenied` even when the signature is valid. Token claims: `agent, root{tools,resources,intents,max_depth,time_budget_seconds}, chain[{tools,resources,intents,time_budget_seconds}], depth, iat, exp` — nothing else. A shared secret = integrity within one trust domain, not attestation: the root is rebuilt from the token, so a holder of the secret can mint any scope at all, root included — the token adds no authority beyond what the holder could grant itself with `scope()`. A rebuilt scope past `exp` refuses `attenuate()`/`to_token()` (`ScopeTokenError("expired")`); `scope.assert_active()` / `scope.expired` for long-held scopes.

## Watch decisions live

- `watchlight dev` → serves a local dashboard at `http://127.0.0.1:7000` that tails `.watchlight/audit.jsonl`: ALLOW/DENY feed, the attenuation tree, and MCP decisions. Flags: `--port`, `--host`, `--no-open`.

## Test policies before they gate real actions

- `govern.test([{ "name": ..., "action": ..., "principal"?: ..., "resource"?: ..., "context"?: {...}, "approved"?: true, "expect": "Allow"|"Deny"|"NeedsApproval" }, ...])` → runs golden fixtures against the loaded policies; returns `{ total, passed, failed, results: [{name, expected, actual, ok, reason}] }`. Drives the engine's decision core directly, so it **never writes the audit trail** and holds zero decision logic. A verdict mismatch is a failed result; a fixture missing `action`/`expect` raises. `"approved": true` mints a single-use token and asserts the human-confirmed `NeedsApproval → Allow` downgrade. `"obligations": { "redact"?: [...], "maxItems"|"max_items"?: n, "logValues"|"log_values"?: bool, "extra"?: {name: raw | [raw, ...]} }` additionally asserts the obligations the `Allow` carries — exact match (`redact` as a set, `extra` per key as a set of values, a string standing for a one-element set; `{}` = none); a `null` value is ill-typed, not absent; an ill-typed expectation, or a non-empty one on a `Deny`/`NeedsApproval` fixture, is a malformed suite (raises / exit 2). Results gain `obligations` (actual) and `expectedObligations` / `expected_obligations`. (Node: `await govern.test([...])`.) Requires `watchlight >= 0.5.0` / `@watchlight/sdk >= 0.5.0`.
- `watchlight policy test suite.json` → CLI for CI; `suite.json` is `{ "policyFile"?: "watchlight.policy.json", "policies"?: [{name,code}], "tests": [...] }`. Exit 0 all-pass, 1 on any verdict mismatch, 2 on a malformed suite. Node: `npx watchlight policy test suite.json`.

## Govern an MCP server — the `watchlight-mcp` package

- `import watchlight_mcp`
- `watchlight_mcp.serve(listen_addr="127.0.0.1:9700", upstream_url="http://localhost:3000/mcp", upstream_server="github", policy_files=[...], audit_path=...)` — front a **Streamable-HTTP** MCP server. Point your MCP client at `http://127.0.0.1:9700/mcp`. Blocks until Ctrl-C. Optional native TLS (`watchlight-mcp >= 0.4.0`): `tls_cert=`/`tls_key=` terminate HTTPS on the listener; `upstream_ca=` trusts a private/self-signed `https://` upstream (fails closed without it).
- `watchlight_mcp.serve_background(...) -> handle` — non-blocking `serve()`; returns a handle with `.reload_policies([files])` (atomic hot-swap; fails closed if the new set doesn't compile), `.stop()`, and `.running`. Same parameters (including TLS) as `serve()`. Requires `watchlight-mcp >= 0.3.0`.
- `watchlight_mcp.serve_stdio(upstream_command=["python","-m","mcp_server_git","-r","/repo"], upstream_server="git", agent_id=None, principal_id=None, policy_files=[...], audit_path=...)` — govern a **stdio-launched** MCP server (the common case). Requires `watchlight-mcp >= 0.2.0`. All logs/audit go to stderr because stdout is the protocol wire.
- The PEP governs the acting methods — `tools/call`, `resources/read`, `resources/subscribe`, `prompts/get` — authorizing each in-process before it can reach the upstream; a denied call never leaves the PEP. The tool/resource/prompt target lands in `context.mcp.tool` / `context.mcp.uri` / `context.mcp.prompt` for policies. Routing headers (`Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name`) are optional — the JSON-RPC body is authoritative; a present-but-mismatched header is rejected.

## Runtime context, per-call principal, and human-in-the-loop (0.4.0 — Python + TS)

- **Runtime context + per-call principal:** bind per-call facts into Cedar and set the acting user. Python `@govern.tool(intent="book", principal=lambda a: f'User::"{a["userId"]}"', context=lambda a: {"amount": a["amount"], "limit": a["limit"]})`; TS `govern.tool(fn, { intent, principal, resource, context })` — each of `principal`/`resource`/`context` is a value or a function of the call args. Policies can then gate on `context.amount <= context.limit` and `principal == User::"..."`. (Only the DE-supported Cedar operators resolve: `context.*`, `==`, `is`, `like`, set `.contains()`.)
- **Low-level primitive:** Python `govern.authorize(action=, principal=, resource=, context=, approval=)`, TS `govern.authorize({ action, principal?, resource?, context?, approval? })` → `{decision: "Allow"|"Deny"|"NeedsApproval", allowed, needs_approval, approved, decision_id, reason}`. `decision_id` (the engine `request_id`) is also written to the audit line — join it to your own booking/order/record.
- **Obligations on an Allow:** a `permit` annotated `@obligate_redact("ssn, dob")` / `@obligate_max_items("25")` / `@obligate_log_values("false")` / any other `@obligate_<name>("raw")` yields `obligations` on the result — Python `result["obligations"] = {"redact": [...], "max_items": n, "log_values": bool, "extra": {name: [raw, ...]}}`, TS `d.obligations = { redact, maxItems, logValues, extra: Record<string, string[]> }` (each key only when set; the whole field absent when none). Constraints the caller MUST honour (strip those fields, cap the batch, don't log values) — typically in `on_result` / `onResult`. **Only an Allow carries them** (an approved one included); `Deny` and `NeedsApproval` never do. Every carrier — the engine's merged `details.obligations` and each determining permit's `policy_results[].obligations` — merges to the strictest reading: `redact` union, `max_items` min, `log_values` AND; `extra` values are raw and uninterpreted, so `extra[name]` lists every distinct value (sorted) and your code decides what a disagreement means. A known obligation the SDK cannot read (e.g. `max_items: "8"`) is never dropped: `authorize` raises/throws `AuthorizeError` with the fixed message `"invalid obligations on an Allow decision"` and a governed tool body does not run. Values are policy-authored strings — never derived from request or result data. Treat a missing obligation as no permission, not no limit (`maxItems ?? 0`). Requires `@watchlight/engine` / `watchlight-engine` >= 0.2.0 (the SDK's dependency); an older engine emits no field at all.
- **Human-in-the-loop:** a permit annotated `@enforcement_effect("require_approval")` yields **NeedsApproval** (not Allow/Deny). Get a human confirmation, then `mint_approval(action=, resource=)` (Python) / `govern.mintApproval({ action, resource })` (TS) → a single-use, TTL, resource-bound token; re-authorize with `approval=token` / `{ approval }` to proceed. `govern.tool(..., on_needs_approval=)` / `{ onNeedsApproval }` runs this inline. Fail-closed: unconfirmed → raises `NeedsApproval` (Python) / throws `NeedsApproval` (TS); the body never runs. DE tokens are local HMAC; Enterprise KMS-signs them into signed lineage.

## Govern what a tool RETURNS — egress hook (Python + TS)

- `@govern.tool(intent, ..., on_result=hook)` (Python) / `govern.tool(fn, { intent, onResult })` (TS): `hook(result, info)` runs AFTER the body returns and BEFORE the caller sees the result, with `info = {intent, resource, principal, decision_id, obligations}` (TS `{ intent, resource, principal, decisionId, obligations? }`) — the SAME id written on the call's decision record, plus the obligations of that decision — the key is present only when the Allow carries any (both lanes; Python: read it with `info.get("obligations")`). `governTool` / `governTools` and the `governedHooks` `PostToolUse` hook populate it the same way. Use it to `sanitize`, screen, honour the obligations, or run a second `authorize` on the result's classification (e.g. `action: "release"`, `context: { classification }`). **Return a value → it replaces the payload; return `None` / `undefined` / `null` → passthrough; raise/throw → the payload is withheld (fail-closed): the error propagates, the raw result is never returned.** Python: an async hook requires an async tool body (on a sync body it is refused fail-closed with `TypeError`, payload withheld). Writes a value-free `egress` audit record `{ts, agent, principal, intent, event: "egress", resource, replaced, decision_id}` (+ `withheld: true` on a throw/timeout) — never the result. No hook → no record.
- Same option on the TS adapters: `governTool(tool, { intent, onResult })` / `governTools(tools, { onResult })`; `governedHooks({ onResult, onResultTimeoutMs? })` installs a Claude Agent SDK `PostToolUse` hook — a returned value becomes `updatedToolOutput` (what the model sees); a throw, or outrunning the internal deadline (default 8000 ms; the SDK matcher `timeout` is set to `ceil(ms/0.8)` s so ours fires first), replaces the output with the opaque `"not authorized"`. Joined to the PreToolUse decision by `tool_use_id`; without one, no `decision_id` on the egress record. Pattern: `examples/patterns/egress-after-read.md`.

## Redact PII before an agent reads a document (sanitize, 0.3.0 — Python + TS)

- `govern.sanitize(text, ...)` (Python) / `govern.sanitize(text, {...})` (TS) — deterministic redaction on **extracted text** (extract a PDF/DOCX to text first; never hand the agent the original file — its hidden layers leak). Detects EMAIL, PHONE, SSN, CREDIT_CARD (Luhn-validated), IBAN, IPV4, API_KEY, PASSPORT (labelled numbers + MRZ lines), DOB (labelled dates of birth) — `DETECTOR_VERSION = "de-rules-2"`. `known: [...]` / `known=[...]` redacts an app-supplied dictionary of exact values (case-insensitive, every occurrence, counted as KNOWN; values never leave the process). PERSON and ADDRESS are opt-in, lower-precision heuristics (off by default; list them in `types`). Modes: `tag` (consistent `<EMAIL_1>`, default), `mask` (`[EMAIL]`), `hash`. Returns the redacted text + a **value-free** report (counts by type + mode — never the values), and writes a value-free `sanitization` audit record. Pass `decision_id=` (Python) / `{ decisionId }` (TS) from the `authorize` decision that governed the read: it is echoed on the report and written as `decision_id` on the `sanitization` audit line, so it joins the decision's line on the same key (opaque, 1–128 chars — UTF-16 code units in TS, code points in Python — no control or line-separator characters; otherwise `SanitizeError`). Fail-closed. A pure `sanitize(...)` is also exported; recall is bounded by the enabled detectors.

## Screen retrieved content before it reaches the model (screen — Python + TS)

- `govern.screen(text, ...)` (Python) / `govern.screen(text, {...})` (TS) — deterministic, rule-based detection of prompt-injection / output-leak shapes in text the agent reads but did not write (web pages, search and tool results) or in what the model produced. Seven families, each a named counter in the report: `INSTRUCTION_OVERRIDE`, `ROLE_SWITCH`, `PROMPT_EXFILTRATION`, `JAILBREAK_MARKER`, `AUTHORITY_IMPERSONATION`, `HTML_INJECTION`, `PROMPT_LEAK`. Modes: `report` (default — text untouched, counts only), `redact` (matched spans → `[FAMILY]`). Report is **value-free**: `{mode, detector_version ("de-screen-1"), counts, total, flagged}` — never the matched text or offsets; writes a value-free `screening` audit record. Pass `decision_id=` (Python) / `{ decisionId }` (TS) from the `authorize` decision that governed the read: it is echoed on the report and written as `decision_id` on the `screening` line, so it joins the decision (same bounds as `sanitize`: opaque, 1–128 chars, no control characters — otherwise `ScreenError`). Fail-closed (`ScreenError` with fixed messages on a non-string, unknown mode / family, empty family list, or malformed `decision_id`). Matching ignores case, whitespace runs and zero-width characters; it does NOT decode leetspeak, homoglyphs or encodings, and text that quotes an attack verbatim is flagged. `redact` marks the trigger (a whole `<script>…</script>` element when its body has no `<`) — it does not neutralise HTML; markers can be spoofed by input, so decide from the report, not the text. Call it inside the governed tool body before returning (throw `Denied(toolName, intent, DENY_REASON)` to refuse), or in the `onResult` / `on_result` egress hook of `govern.tool`. Known TS/Python divergence: Turkish dotted capital İ case-folds only in Python. Pattern: [screen-before-model](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/blob/main/examples/patterns/screen-before-model.md).

## TypeScript / Node lane — `@watchlight/sdk` (verified, 0.5.0)

- `import { govern, Denied, NeedsApproval } from "@watchlight/sdk";` — same default governor, fail-closed, value-free `.watchlight/audit.jsonl`. `govern.tool(fn, {intent})` is a **higher-order function** (not a decorator) and returns an async function.
- `govern.allow('permit(...);')` / `govern.load("policies.json")`; `govern.tool(fn, { intent, principal?, resource?, context?, onNeedsApproval?, onResult? })`; `govern.authorize({...})`; `govern.mintApproval({...})`; `govern.sanitize(text, {...})`; `govern.screen(text, {...})`.
- Framework adapters: `governedHooks({ intentFor, onResult? })` → Claude Agent SDK `hooks` (PreToolUse gate; PostToolUse egress when `onResult` is set); `governTool(tool, { intent, onResult? })` / `governTools(tools, { intentFor, onResult? })` → LangChain / LangGraph.js `StructuredTool` governance. `govern.scope().attenuate()` → strict-subset sub-agent scopes (`DE_MAX_DEPTH` 5); `scope.toToken()` / `await govern.scopeFromToken(token)` carry a scope to another process (`new Watchlight({ tokenSecret })` or `WATCHLIGHT_TOKEN_SECRET`; the receiving engine replays the chain; `ScopeTokenError` on a bad token, `AttenuationDenied` on a widened one).
- Graduation: set `WATCHLIGHT_APDP_URL` (+ `WATCHLIGHT_PLUGIN_TOKEN`, `WATCHLIGHT_TENANT_ID`) to run the same code against the networked control plane; `govern.mode` → `"in-process"` | `"networked"`.
- Packages: `@watchlight/sdk` (Apache-2.0 glue) depends on `@watchlight/engine` (the compiled engine). Node ≥ 18. Docs: https://docs.watchlight.ai/de/typescript

## Docs (narrative guides on docs.watchlight.ai/de)

- [Overview](https://docs.watchlight.ai/de/): what DE is, the package map, and where it fits the progressive-deployment model.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.watchlight.ai/de/quickstart): `pip install`, govern a tool, print your first ALLOW/DENY in under five minutes.
- [TypeScript / Node](https://docs.watchlight.ai/de/typescript): `npm install @watchlight/sdk`, govern a tool in-process, runtime context + human-in-the-loop, Claude Agent SDK + LangGraph.js adapters.
- [Cedar policy syntax](https://docs.watchlight.ai/de/policies): the policy language the engine evaluates, from first principles.
- [Governed agents (in-process)](https://docs.watchlight.ai/de/governed-agents): govern an agent lifecycle with `InProcessClient` (from `watchlight-agent-sdk` / `watchlight_core`).
- [Sub-agent scope attenuation](https://docs.watchlight.ai/de/scope-attenuation): strict-subset confinement, the depth-5 ceiling, and the deepagents example.
- [Govern an MCP server](https://docs.watchlight.ai/de/mcp-server): `serve` (HTTP) and `serve_stdio` (stdio) transports.
- [Enforcement effects](https://docs.watchlight.ai/de/enforcement-effects): what a policy can do beyond allow/deny.
- [Field reference](https://docs.watchlight.ai/de/reference): the request/response shape and what is enforced vs advisory.
- [Developer Edition vs Enterprise](https://docs.watchlight.ai/de/comparison): what the control plane adds and when to reach for it.

## Runnable examples (in the repo)

- [agent.py](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/blob/main/examples/agent.py): the smallest governed agent — the DENY line, zero infra.
- [showcase/denied-before-execute](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/tree/main/examples/showcase/denied-before-execute): governed transfer against a stub bank with a call counter; a `forbid` above a threshold is refused before the body runs and the counter is asserted 0 (Python + TS; `policy.suite.json` doubles as the golden tests).
- [showcase/human-in-the-loop](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/tree/main/examples/showcase/human-in-the-loop): `NeedsApproval` → pending request on disk → separate `approve.py`/`approve.mjs` signs a grant → `resume` runs once with an `approved: true` record joined to the pending one; grant and token replays refused (Python + TS).
- [governed_research_agent.py](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/blob/main/examples/governed_research_agent.py): a multi-tool agent governed by intent.
- [governed_subagents.py](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/blob/main/examples/governed_subagents.py): scope attenuation — every child a strict subset of its parent.
- [governed_deepagents.py](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/blob/main/examples/governed_deepagents.py): governing a [deepagents](https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents) deep agent via `govern.scope` (runs without an API key).
- [governed_langgraph_agent.py](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/blob/main/examples/governed_langgraph_agent.py) · [governed_pydantic_ai_agent.py](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/blob/main/examples/governed_pydantic_ai_agent.py) · [governed_claude_agent.py](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/blob/main/examples/governed_claude_agent.py): framework plugins, governed in-process.
- [governed_mcp_server.py](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/blob/main/examples/governed_mcp_server.py): a policy enforcement point in front of an MCP server.
- [context_governance.py](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/blob/main/examples/context_governance.py): policy-based content/PII screening.
- [showcase/policy-tests-ci/](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/tree/main/examples/showcase/policy-tests-ci): policy suites as a CI gate — a GitHub Actions workflow template running `watchlight policy test` (TypeScript and Python CLIs), plus a widened policy variant that fails the suite.
- [showcase/audit-forensics/](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/tree/main/examples/showcase/audit-forensics): reconstruct who did what from `audit.jsonl` — generators for a trail with every record kind, `forensics.py` and jq recipes that join on `decision_id`; exact field names per record kind.
- [showcase/poisoned-rag/](https://github.com/watchlight-ai-beacon/watchlight-de/blob/main/examples/showcase/poisoned-rag/README.md) (`rag.py` + `rag.mjs`): a RAG pipeline where one retrieved document hides a prompt injection and personal data — `screen()` withholds it in the `on_result` hook, the permit's `@obligate_redact` obligation drives `sanitize()` for what passes, and decision / screening / sanitization / egress records join on one `decision_id`; self-asserting, exits non-zero on failure.
- Policy files live beside them: `watchlight.policy.json`, `research.policy.json`, `framework.policy.json`, `mcp.policy.json`.

## Gotchas for coding agents (get these right)

- **Fail-closed.** No policy = every governed call is denied. You must `govern.load(...)` or `govern.allow(...)` a permit before anything runs.
- **A `@govern.tool` resource is `tool/<function_name>`.** Write policies against that resource, e.g. `permit(principal, action == Action::"research", resource == Resource::"tool/web_search");` — or leave `resource` unconstrained.
- **Framework plugins authorize as `Agent::"<uuid>"`, not your run label.** A policy that pins `principal == User::"research-agent"` will NOT match a plugin-governed run and every action is denied. Gate framework-agent policies on the **action/resource**, or on `principal is Agent` — never a hardcoded principal id you can't know in advance. (The low-level `InProcessClient.authorize("research-agent", ...)` DOES use the label you pass — that's the one place a `User::"..."` principal matches.)
- **`serve()` fronts HTTP MCP servers; `serve_stdio()` fronts stdio ones.** Never pass a `stdio://` string as `upstream_url` to `serve()`: on `watchlight-mcp >= 0.2.1` it is rejected at startup with a clear error; on earlier versions it binds and then fails as a late 502 on the first allowed call. Use `serve_stdio(upstream_command=[...])` for a stdio-launched server.
- **`watchlight dev` needs a free port (default 7000); `serve()` needs its listen port free.** DE keeps no process registry — you own port hygiene. A stale orphaned server can hold a port and silently produce an empty audit.
- **Cedar string idioms:** the engine resolves `context.*`, `==`, `is`, `like` (glob), and `set.contains()`. It does **not** have `.startsWith()` / `.contains()` on strings — use `like "prefix*"`. Entity-attribute reads and `in` hierarchy are not part of the DE engine surface; a policy that relies on them silently denies.
- **Audit is value-free by contract.** Argument *values* never enter `.watchlight/audit.jsonl` — only who, what intent, which resource, and the decision. Don't expect to read tool arguments back out of it.
